claims.text: The initial high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution.
The initial alloy exhibits a favorable strength–ductility combination.
A controlled amount of grain-boundary-pinning particles can be introduced into the alloy.
The proposed thermal exposure is 800 °C for 100 hours.
Thermal exposure is followed by tensile loading at room temperature.
Grain-boundary-pinning particles inhibit grain growth during thermal exposure.
Grain-boundary-pinning particles reduce the formation of detrimental precipitates during thermal exposure.
Inhibiting grain growth and reducing detrimental precipitate formation preserves the alloy's toughness.
After the specified exposure, the particle-containing alloy will have higher toughness than the same alloy without particles under otherwise identical conditions.
Particle amount, type, distribution, and morphology may affect the outcome.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify tensile loading, whereas the principal example of toughness measurement is Charpy impact energy. These are distinct loading modes, so the decisive loading and toughness-testing protocol is not internally aligned.
